title: 《新蝙蝠侠2》新路透：蝙蝠车与哥谭警方街头冲突
text:
相关文章: 《新蝙蝠侠2》已开拍，蝙蝠车出现在格拉斯哥
《新蝙蝠侠2》最新片场视频显示，蝙蝠车在格拉斯哥搭建的哥谭市街道上，与哥谭市警察和SWAT特警展开高速追逐和激烈冲突。
上周，网友拍摄的蝙蝠车片场视频首次在网上曝光。最近，又有人发现一名神秘金发女性坐在蝙蝠车副驾驶座上——她是否就是斯嘉丽·约翰逊，目前还不清楚。 还有更多相关内容 电影《新蝙蝠侠2》「摄像机测试」先导预告
此外，片场粉丝还拍到了一处与第一部电影呼应的细节：哥谭市出租车上出现了反毒品广告，其中提到了第一部电影中的虚构毒品「drops」。
如今，社交媒体上又出现了多段新视频。画面显示，伴随着巨大的引擎轰鸣声，蝙蝠车在格拉斯哥（或者说「哥谭市」）铺着假雪的街道上原地漂移。
随后，哥谭市警局车辆开始追赶蝙蝠车，GCPD还一度将其团团包围。另一段视频中，SWAT特警甚至在近距离直接向蝙蝠车开火。还有画面显示，一辆SWAT车辆曾直接撞向蝙蝠车。
马特·里夫斯执导的第一部《新蝙蝠侠》中，蝙蝠侠与GCPD之间虽然关系紧张，但最终仍建立起了有效合作，尤其是他与戈登警督之间的关系。
电影结尾，蝙蝠侠从谜语人的袭击中救下了市长和其他市民，哥谭公众对这名超级英雄的态度似乎也开始逐渐转向支持。
因此，如今片场中出现警察追赶并向蝙蝠车开火的场景，显然表明蝙蝠侠和GCPD之间的联盟已经恶化。蝙蝠侠现在似乎被当成了一名逃犯。至于这是否意味着他和戈登本人也已经站在对立面，目前仍有待确认。
蝙蝠侠是否在这里遭到了栽赃？还是黑暗骑士已经过度自行其是，让哥谭当局无法继续容忍？目前答案仍然未知。尽管网络上一直流传着大量传闻，但《新蝙蝠侠2》的官方剧情信息至今仍然非常有限。
塞巴斯蒂安·斯坦可能会饰演哈维·登特，也可能不会。科林·法瑞尔饰演的企鹅人则只会在电影中出现几个场景。影片的冬季背景甚至让一些粉丝猜测，急冻人可能会登场。
至于真相究竟如何，只能等到《新蝙蝠侠2》于2028年2月18日正式上映后揭晓。

title: Ray Chase, the voice of Cyclops in X-Men '97, has '1,000 freaking hours' in Slay the Spire and is running a 'smell build' in Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2: ' I wear perfumes and walk into battle with my fancy boy outfit'
text:
Disk Cleanup
(Image credit: Future) Welcome to Disk Cleanup , our regular weekend feature delving into the PCs of PC gaming luminaries. Come back every weekend to read a new interview, digging into the important questions, like "How tidy is your desktop?" and "What game will you never uninstall?"
Ray Chase's first encounter with PC gaming was on an old DOS computer from his father's accounting job. He grew up on a digital diet of shareware demos from PC gaming's golden era. "My grandfather gave me this basket of shareware games, and we played them nonstop for years," Chase recalls. "There was Duke Nukem 1 and 2. There was Ken's Labyrinth. Blake Stone: Aliens of Gold. There was Wolfenstein 3D , of course. Jack Pack was one of my favourites because it had a level editor."
A voice actor since the early 2000s, Chase has appeared in hundreds of games, films and TV shows. He played the lead character Noctis in Final Fantasy 15 , and currently voices Cyclops in X-Men '97, which just aired season two and is in the process of recording season four: "The stuff that's going on in the seasons we're recording now, I guess we'll see in a couple of years, but it's really cool, man."
Chase is also the co-founder of Sassy Chap Games, developer of 2025's Date Everything . A dating sim where players can romance dozens of anthropomorphised household objects, Date Everything was designed to be a celebration of voice acting talent. "We just finished our big update for Date Everything and we are working hard on the next chapter of our story," Chase says. "We're in the pitching process for that now."
Chase took a break from designing romanceable soft furnishings to show me around the hunk-strewn household of his Steam library. Gather round for a tale of perfumed peasants, disordered dungeons, and plane potatoes.
What game are you currently playing?
(Image credit: Deep Silver) I'm currently playing Deltarune Chapter 5, but not [for] super long. The other one that I have is Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 . It's the eternal game. I'm doing all of the things. It'll be a few hundred hours. But it's the perfect encapsulation of what a roleplaying game should be.
I played one [campaign] all the way through. The [most recent] one I've made, I'm doing a smell build where your character smells and looks so good and fancy that it actually works as armour. And so I wear perfumes and walk into battle with my fancy boy outfit. And my enemies are too stunned.
I'm always laundering my clothes. It's the best. I just fucking love that game.
What was the previous game you played, and is it still installed?
(Image credit: Yacht Club Games) I played Mina the Hollower . I love that game, my God. Jay Kaufman's music is astounding. I played that one out of order because I saw you could do that, and I really liked the challenge. So I did the dungeons all in the wrong order. I really enjoyed the feeling of doing a really hard dungeon and then going back and then saying "Oh, this is now very easy" going through it.
I also love that [Mina is] middle aged like me, and after she completes a dungeon she goes to sleep. She takes a nap, which I think is great.
I'm not a secret ending kind of guy. I'm whatever my percentage is when I complete the game. That's what I live with, and that's it. I never go back and play games. [With] Disco Elysium , the best thing about it is the cryptozoologist thing, the cryptid comes at the end and says something incredible. But I [failed the roll]. And so I will never know what it is. I'm never going to go back and play it, and I won't look it up either.
I think that's part of the fun, living with the consequences.
What is the oldest game (by release date) currently installed on your PC?
(Image credit: Blobfish) I've got Brotato here. I have very little on my PC, that's the problem. I love Brotato. It's one of my favourites. It's because it's so lightweight. It's great for planes, and you don't need a controller to play. I end up playing on my laptop on planes more than anything.
Anything that's super lightweight, I'll always have [installed]. So it's going to be Brotato. I 100%-ed it before the newest DLC, which makes it really hard.
There's so many different potatoes you can be. There's so many different playstyles. I'll take whatever comes my way. It's never old. Same with Slay the Spire … there's always something different, always something new to learn, and I absolutely adore it.
Oh, maybe Slay the Spire is older than Brotato. So then, that's my answer.
What is the highest number of hours you have in any given game, according to Steam?
It's Slay the Spire for sure. It is something like 600 hours. But then I've got it on mobile too, and I also got all the way to the end with all characters.
I got into it very early on. I went to a gathering and some guy was like "There's this early access game named Slay the Spire, you should give it a shot." There was only Ironclad and Silent at the time. I don't know if it was [in] early access then, or if it was just a demo version. But I was there from almost the very, very beginning.
I'd never played a deckbuilder before, and it was the best. I played it all the way through to release to Watcher, 1,000 freaking hours in that thing. And it's easy to 100% that game. The achievements are not very difficult, but I do love Ascension, getting Ascension on all characters and then beating it on Ascension 20. That to me is the correct difficulty.
What game will you never, ever uninstall?
Brotato or Slay the Spire. They're just always there, for when I'm on the plane and I'll be able to give it a quick spin.
What's a piece of non-gaming software installed on your PC that you simply couldn't live without?
(Image credit: Musegroup) My voice recording software for sure. That's pretty simple.
I use Reaper and Audacity , [they] are my two favourites. And I absolutely could not live without voice recording software.
That would be impossible.
How tidy is your desktop screen?
Extremely tidy. There's almost nothing on it. It's just the audio that I recorded this morning before coming into this interview, and then my Recycle Bin. And that's it, it's empty. I don't like having a bunch of stuff that I don't know where the hell it is.
[I'm a] one-screen guy. Sometimes I have my second screen up here when I'm recording, but today it's just my laptop and nothing else fancy. This laptop is the laptop I developed Date Everything on.

title: EverQuest Legends dev says 'I'm sure we would' add new classes, races 'in the longer-term vision of the game'
text:
EverQuest Legends, the EverQuest spinoff that remixes an old-school version of the early MMORPG into a multiclassing, froglok-murdering ARPG minmaxer's paradise , has a lot on the way. In a recent Twitch stream , developers from Daybreak Games and Game Jawn floated some pretty big ideas for the future: perhaps most notably, all-new classes that weren't in the original EverQuest at all.
"Definitely, I think, long-term we have discussed additional races, additional classes. Is it realistic to have another class by [the upcoming expansion] Kunark? I don't think so," said Daybreak executive producer David Youssefi. "But definitely would not rule it out for the longer-term vision of the game. In fact, I'm sure we would." Game Jawn CEO and technical director Eda Spause chimed in, "Yeah, absolutely."
Granted, they were careful to temper expectations. Before Youssefi said that, lead content designer Eric Wellman addressed the topic by saying it's "a matter of how much work, and is it worth the work." Spause replied, "I'm of the opinion it would be, however, that opinion is also at odds with the reality of how much we have to do." In other words, this is less a guarantee and more an optimistic plan for the future.
While, for the most part, Legends is just a casual-friendly remix of an old game, this particular long-term ambition calls to mind Old School RuneScape and the oft-rumored 'Classic+' version of World of Warcraft taking after the game's private server scene . Every class playable in even the modern version of the original EverQuest is already represented, so the addition of new classes would see Legends join the chorus of MMOs and live service games building new stuff using an old version as scaffolding.
And while Legends already has an original playable race in the catlike kerran and revamped zones here and there, I'd argue new playstyles are the bigger deal in a game all about concocting builds and farming phat loots. As for what those classes would even be, it's hard to say.
EverQuest has so many classic D&D-style fantasies represented that it started splitting hairs between wizards and magicians—pretty thematically narrow things like beastlords and berserkers made it in eventually. I'm sure EverQuest 2 can provide some inspiration, what with its coercers, defilers, and other sub-classes with oddly vague names.
In the meantime, check out PC Gamer news writer Joshua Wolens' impressions on EverQuest Legends, where he called the game "an MMO for MUD enjoyers and Morrowind perverts—no longer hard, but still authentically idiosyncratic … the Linux of MMOs."

title: It's been 25 years and I'm still not over one of the greatest songs to grace JRPGs
text:
Critical Hit
(Image credit: Future) Welcome to Critical Hit , where I (or someone else on the PC Gamer team) celebrate and lament all things videogame music, audio design, and the ways our favourite games make our ears tingle.
Last month, Final Fantasy 10 turned 25 years old—a fact that has utterly shaken my perception of the passage of time, leaving me to slowly decay into a pile of dust. It remains one of my favourite JRPGs of all time, even if PC only has the significantly weirder-looking, plastic-faced HD remaster. The romance! The belts! The turn-based battling! The cutscenes! Things that all still very much hold up two-and-a-half decades later, in my humble and not at all biased opinion.
But one aspect that has endured above all others is the game's soundtrack. It's this immaculate blend of genres, something we'd see happen more in future games like Final Fantasy 13-2. From the all-out rock of Otherworld that blasts your ears during the introduction of Blitzball rockstar Tidus, to the wonderfully ethereal Besaid. Or even the game's overarching theme, To Zanarkand, which is the perfect musical embodiment of its melancholic narrative.
When I think about Final Fantasy 10, though, one song always comes to mind: Suteki Da Ne. It's the song that plays during a hugely pivotal moment in the game. Yuna has become increasingly conflicted over her role as a summoner—one which is destined to end in her death—but her desire to quit is outweighed by her commitment to her duty.
The scene culminates in her and Tidus together in the springs at Macalania Woods, a gorgeous glittering landscape painted in shades of blue, while the two descend under the water and share a kiss. It's the first display of romantic intimacy between the two, capped off by the delicate Japanese vocals and sweet orchestra of Suteki Da Ne.
It wasn't the series' first attempt at a vocal track. Final Fantasy 6 had pseudo-vocals during the famous opera scene. Final Fantasy 7, of course, had One Winged Angel, and Final Fantasy 8 was the first time I recall a vocal song in the series going more pop-focused with Eyes on Me.
But Final Fantasy 10, being the first to release on PlayStation 2, felt like a huge step up in terms of how hard composer Nobuo Uematsu could cook. It's a song that's needed little-to-no rearrangement in the years since, because it remains so dang good from its initial conception.
It's the first vocal track I remember really resonating with in a Final Fantasy game, one that brought me to tears the way no other videogame had up until that point. It feels beautiful and tragic at the same time, and it's a track I don't think a game in the series has ever come close to matching since—though Final Fantasy 14's Flow is probably the closest contender.
I'm not sure we'll ever get another soundtrack quite like Final Fantasy 10, and 25 years later I still find myself going back to its music time and time again. And while Suteki Da Ne might not be my most listened to of the bunch, I maintain it's one of the best composed pieces—a diamond in a huge stinkin' pile of gold. And one that still brings a little tear to my eye every time I listen to it.

title: 'We didn't have layoffs before, and now all of a sudden we have yearly layoffs': Bethesda artist says 'something has changed' under Microsoft
text:
Last week, the Communications Workers of America and the Bethesda Game Studios OneBGS union took part in the Save Our Devs rally across the United States and Canada (and on Twitch ) "to call out layoffs and corporate greed across the industry and to demand fair first contracts across Microsoft’s gaming studios." Speaking to Kotaku , Bethesda artist Alex Nguyen talked about how things changed after Bethesda was acquired by the tech giant.
"Since we’ve been under Microsoft… it feels like something has changed. We didn’t have layoffs before, and now all of a sudden we have yearly layoffs," he told Kotaku, saying teams were feeling the effects of cuts which eroded institutional knowledge. “If only five people knew how this thing worked and you let all five of them go, that’s a morale killer because it’s like we already knew this, and now we have to learn it again.”
According to that article, Nguyen pointed out that fixer-uppers like Fallout 76 and Elder Scrolls Online don't get a chance to bloom into successful fan favorites without sufficient labor and time. He also noted that there used to be a shared sense of long-term commitment among the staff at Zenimax and Bethesda—a commitment being smothered by Microsoft's current corporate tactics.
“That’s why a lot of people had such a long tenure here," Nguyen told Kotaku. "And they were like, ‘yeah, this is the place I’m gonna retire at,’ or ‘this is the place where I’m gonna finish out,’ or ‘I love being here because I want to stay in the industry for a long time.’ That was basically one of the benefits of being at Bethesda or a Zenimax studio in general.”
Last year, ex-Xbox head Phil Spencer said that " nurturing and protecting creative teams that want to go take risks " was of the utmost importance less than two years after Xbox's acquisition of Blizzard called for 1,900 layoffs . Current Xbox head Asha Sharma has sung a similar tune so far, suggesting that Xbox ought to be entertaining over a billion people each day while also announcing the "reset" necessitating 3,200 job cuts in the very same blog post . It's plain to see why workers might balk at conditions that continue to raise the bar for achievement while more and more developers lose their livelihoods.

title: Steam Week in Review: A touch of AI is all it takes to trigger backlash, as a promising new indie falls afoul of slop skeptics
text:
Vapor World: Over The Mind is a Soulslike Metroidvania with an evocative, painterly art style reminiscent of Lies of P and the narrative platformers of Playdead. According to Korean studio Alive Inc, the game had 100,000 wishlists just before its early access launch on August 19, mostly on the strength of a demo available since January 2025.
But what should have been a triumphant early access launch went pear shaped very quickly. At launch, few talked about the quite distinctive worldbuilding or the parry-heavy combat. Instead, all focus was trained entirely on something absent from the popular demo: very obvious AI use.
"Saw the very first cutscene, before any gameplay, and how the generative AI they used couldn't even keep the main character's model consistent," reads the "most helpful" Steam review for Vapor World. "From the trailers the gameplay looked pretty fun [but] unfortunately I support people not robots. If the look you want to go for is beyond the scope you can achieve right now then I suggest you change it or wait until you can produce the art and style you want with people doing it."
That's pretty representative of the Steam reviews at the moment: Vapor World is currently sitting on 64 "mostly negative" reviews.
It's undoubtedly a disappointing result for Alive Inc, whose headcount is " about five " according to the studio. It's also possible the studio was blindsided by the backlash: this Pew Research Center survey places South Korea as the least AI sceptical nation among 25 countries surveyed, including the US, the UK, Australia and India. According to MIT Technology Review , the South Korean government has overwhelmingly embraced AI. It even tried to roll out AI-powered school textbooks (which failed).
Half (or in some cases, slightly less) of those surveyed in the US, Italy, Australia and Brazil are "more concerned than excited" by AI use in daily life. In South Korea, those "more concerned than excited" by AI make up only 16 percent.
There's a trace of surprise in the inevitable statement made by studio director Young Kim, who promised the AI-generated cutscenes would be replaced "by this weekend" (this has already happened).
(Image credit: Alive Inc) "If someone asked me what I think about using AI, the honest answer is that I would have to think about it for a long time," the director wrote. "The reason I chose AI was that I believed it could reach a level of expression our existing resources could not, and that it would let us focus more on the game itself, outside of story and cinematics."
He continued: "That was a hasty judgment on my part. Unless AI takes one more leap and reaches a point where no one can tell the difference, what I believed was still closer to an ideal than a reality. I expected some of you would be disappointed by our use of AI. I did not expect it to become this big."
The statement then hits upon a question that will be raised again and again in the coming months and years concerning creative work: if AI can do it better, why not? In this instance, it unambiguously could not: the cutscenes, and I've seen them, are quintessential slop, and compare very unfavourably to the in-game art. Young Kim says the studio originally composed the cutscenes in-engine, but later replaced them with AI. Somehow, his team didn't detect this chasm.
"The truth is, we spent a long time trying to tell this game's story with cutscenes made entirely by our own hands," the statement goes on. "The results were devastating every time. We came to believe we could not properly deliver this game's complex, difficult narrative that way, and that is why we turned to AI. But if that choice hurt your experience, the fault is not in the tool. It is in our own shortcomings."
Alive Inc joins a long list of studios who have reneged on AI use after extreme public backlash, including Larian Studios and Sandfall Interactive. Vapor World isn't wholesale slop—the studio worked hard on the core game and it shows—but the outcry surrounding its launch does show that using generative AI to cut corners isn't, for now, something audiences are willing to tolerate.

title: Nightdive's Thief remaster unearths a 'very very out of date version control repository' with 'the wildest things to say about the code'
text:
It's great that the Nightdive's remasters of various classic games give new players a chance to experience them without having to download a fixpack or remap the controls or whatever, but it's also a wonderful opportunity to learn new things about games we already loved. Each remaster is like an archaeological dig and you never know what it'll uncover.
Digital Foundry's Retro Super Show recently spoke to Nightdive about their current project, a remaster of Looking Glass Studio's stealth classic Thief: The Dark Project. If you're super into the minutiae of Thief, as you should be, it's a cool insight into the making of the game and in particular, the Dark Engine that powers it.
"There's nothing else like it even to this day," Nightdive software engineer Josh Dowell says. As he explains, Nightdive got to see "a very very out of date version control repository for the code" and that made the origins of its oddities more obvious. "I think most of the team that started working on it ended up moving to different projects and then a whole new team took over for the second half of its development," he says.
Back when it was just called The Dark Project, Thief was shown at E3 in 1997 and scheduled to release later that year. It was soon delayed to 1998, and the comments Dowell found attached to the code make it seem like it was still being worked on as it made its way out the door. "My favorite part of looking through the Dark Engine codebase has been seeing all of the evil comments left by the Looking Glass programmers, all the Irrational Games programmers," he says. "They have the wildest things to say about the code. They say, 'Giant hack! Never replicate this! We must fix this before '98!' 'E3 hack! We must delete this after E3!' and it's still there in Thief 2."
In spite of the rushed and hacky nature of its creation, the Dark Engine is capable of incredible things—feats of audio, AI, and lighting that were cutting edge at the time and still able to impress. Part of why it works so well is what it shares with another boundary-pushing first-person game of the era. "Thief's rendering and the technology that powers the levels is, shockingly, it's just a clone of Quake," Dowell says. "The way they do the lighting is exactly the same as Quake, the way that lights are turned on and off is Quake."
While he calls the two "eerily similar" the differences are "really strange" as he puts it. "So Quake uses precomputed visibility, which means when you're standing in a specific part of the level, the game knows exactly what you can see without having to think about it. But the Dark Engine does what Quake does during its precomputing phase, where every single doorway in the world is a portal and it sees the rectangle that you can see through that portal and it sees the other portals to other doors and then calculates which ones you can see through that portal. It's super complicated and I can't believe they got away with it in '98, because it's doing the thing that Quake did that was slow, but it's doing it in real-time."
Thief: The Dark Project Remastered doesn't have a release date yet, but you can follow its progress on Steam , GOG , and Epic .

title: Twitch hit with class-action lawsuit over Amazon AI training: 'Twitch sent no email, displayed no pop-up notification, and made no announcement'
text:
In yet another unpleasant move in our AI hellscape, Amazon was caught training its generative AI using Twitch stream content earlier this month—a particularly brazen strategy, especially given Twitch's chief product officer admitted that the data collection was opt-out because "nobody would opt in." Hmm, I wonder why!
Anyway, despite attempts to insist that Twitch wasn't doing this, Amazon was —a distinction which pretty much doesn't matter, as Amazon owns Twitch, and even if it didn't, Twitch still would have been permitting this—the streaming platform's caught a ton of flak for trying to slide this one under the table.
Including, per Courthouse News, a class-action lawsuit. Plaintiff Warren Pandiscia, who has around 1,000 followers on the site, claims that "because Amazon AI products are commercialized, Amazon had an overwhelming incentive to acquire training data on an unprecedented scale.
"Rather than negotiate for lawful licenses or seek permission, defendants accessed the Twitch streams and videos to utilize them as a massive dataset necessary to fuel Amazon's AI products."
The full complaint , filed in California, goes on to state: "Defendants' actions were not only unlawful, but an unconscionable attack on the community of content creators whose content is used to fuel the multitrillion-dollar generative AI industry without any compensation."
The complaint also goes on to note that, per Twitch's documentation, a streamer chatting on someone else's stream might have their voice used to train generative AI despite opting out themselves, as whether or not Amazon can scrape your voice is entirely dependent on the host streamer's settings.
"By design, Defendants never obtain—and their systems are incapable of obtaining—the consent of all parties to the communications they capture," the lawsuit argues.
It also accuses Twitch and Amazon of burying the lede on giving proper notice about the feature: "Twitch sent no email, displayed no pop-up notification, and made no announcement before enabling the setting for every account. The setting was instead discovered by a reporter, Zach Bussey."
Whether or not the lawsuit will gain any steam remains to be seen. It's unfortunate, but Amazon is a giant company and might have enough sway to sweep this under the rug—and given its love affair with the technology , it's unlikely to leave Twitch, a goldmine of training data (if you don't give a crap about the people who made it that way) alone. Unless the prophesied AI bubble actually pops , that is.

title: Windows update that breaks some multiplayer games linked to our desire for gaming PCs that light up all the colors of the rainbow
text:
Last week, we covered the very strange occurrence of a bug in the latest Windows update . Yes, a bug in a Windows update, say it isn't so. Unfortunately, this one does incur our wrath of gamers more than most because it leads to some games becoming unresponsive. Games like Arc Raiders, Marvel Tōkon: Fighting Souls, and The Finals. But we might have to look at our obsession with RGB lighting
When the issue first came to light, shortly after the release of KB5121003, the developer of two of those games came out with a theory. Embark Studios chalked the crashes up to a single driver, inpoutx64.sys, and noted you could disable the troublesome file through the Command Prompt.
As it turns out, that was spot on. Microsoft also thinks that inpoutx64.sys is the problem . Or, at the very least, something doesn't quite gel between inpoutx64.sys, the affected games, and the latest Windows update.
The KB5121003 update is seemingly the catalyst of the whole affair. Microsoft downplays it slightly in the wording of its ongoing investigation: "We are presently working to understand the relationship between these RGB components and the games which trigger this issue. We will provide an update when more information is available."
Anyways, Microsoft also notes what it currently believes is the actual cause of the issue, and it's pinning it mostly on RGB lighting.
"Ongoing investigation indicates that this issue is related to peripherals or internal device components which have RGB lighting features. Such devices may install drivers or code components with file names similar to inpoutx64. In systems where these drivers are found, the issue is then triggered by launching certain games."
Microsoft offers a way to disable the driver via the registry. There's a non-zero chance of messing up your entire PC when diving into the registry, so just be vigilant as you make any changes. Microsoft even recommends backing up the whole thing should anything go wrong.
Open the Windows registry. This can be done by opening the start menu and typing "regedit". Select the Registry Editor from the results.
Navigate to the key HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\inpoutx64. This can be done using the folders on the left side of the window, or typing the path into the address line at the top of the window.
NOTE: Ensure you have backed up the registry, as per the important note above. It may be necessary if you need to undo the change in the following steps.
On the right side of the window, find the registry value named Start. Double click this key and enter the number 4 under the field titled Value data.
Close the window and restart your computer.
As Microsoft notes, this may disable some RGB lighting features or mess with the software used to control them. So, while the company tries to figure out what exactly is causing an issue between the games, driver, and update, those affected may have to decide between playing games or their PC looking pretty. Tough call—you could also just rollback your PC to a previous Windows update and wait for a proper fix.

title: Proposed class action lawsuit against Logitech demands money to be given back to customers after $61 million US tariff refund
text:
A proposed class action lawsuit against Logitech is attempting to recover funds that were allegedly "extracted from American consumers" as a result of the Trump administration's tariffs.
The complaint [PDF] is being led by a construction company, SJK Development, and a California resident, both of whom say they bought Logitech mice at higher, tariff-affected prices. It was filed with the US District Court for the Northern District of California, San Jose Division last week (via Ars Technica ).
"This case is an example of a large multinational corporation and its US subsidiary taking advantage of its customers who rely on the integrity of manufacturers to sell products to customers in good faith," the complaint alleges.
"[The defendant] refused to be honest with their customers by raising prices across their product catalog to allegedly account for costs due to tariffs and then failed to return tariff proceeds when the US Supreme Court declared those tariffs unlawful."
While Logitech did not publicly announce price hikes, the complaint makes mention of the company's executives discussing higher prices and profits in regards to offsetting tariffs in its subsequent earnings calls.
(Image credit: Future) "The company’s CFO, Mr. Anversa, attributed the company’s expanded gross margins—up approximately 130 basis points year-over-year in the fourth quarter—in part to Logitech’s United States subsidiary’s pricing actions executed in April 2025." the filing says.
"Mr. Anversa stated that those pricing actions, together with favorable currency movements, more than offset tariffs and promotions."
The Trump administration's IEEPA tariffs were ruled against by the US Supreme Court in February of this year, after it found that the US president did not have the authority to impose them. Since then, Logitech has received a sum of $61 million as part of the refund process. The lawsuit is aiming for a judgement which would force Logitech to give customers a share of the proceeds.
"Logitech has been—and absent relief will continue to be— enriched twice over at its customers’ expense," the filing continues. "Once by the tariff-justified overcharges collected from Plaintiffs and the Class, and again by the government’s refund, with interest, of the very duties those overcharges were represented to cover."
(Image credit: Future) Several other tech companies, including Nintendo , Sony, and Microsoft, have been on the receiving end of similar legal actions related to tariff refunds . Earlier this month, PC cooling company Arctic announced that it would be rolling back prices on its components for US customers , after receiving a refund of its own.
I have reached out to Logitech for comment, and will update this article if any is received. In the meantime, however, I doubt this will be the last proposed class action suit regarding tariff-inflated pricing. Whatever the outcomes, it'll likely be some time before any major resolution comes to pass.

title: There's a looming GPU supply crisis, which means prices are likely to get a whole lot worse. And it's not just because of memory
text:
A couple weeks back I noted that I'd been tracking GPU prices on an almost weekly basis for a year now, and that things have never been worse . Well, PC Partner—one of the biggest manufacturers of graphics cards you've probably never heard of—suggests it's going to get even worse. And probably quickly.
PC Partner makes a ton of graphics cards for its consumer facing brands Zotac, Inno3D, and Manli. I've visited one of its main factories in Dongguan, China, and it's production lines are big. So when Singaporean outlet, The Straits Times , notes the company as saying that the supply of graphics cards is going to get real tight in the coming months it's worth listening.
And the worst part about it is that apparently it's going to be the entry level cards that will be the most adversely affected. With severe shortages comes increased prices, and while Nvidia cards with VRAM capacities of 8 GB haven't had the spiking price tags of their more heavily memory'd cousins, it looks like it won't be long before they do.
Benchlife, reporting on the PC Partner announcement , has itself confirmed that supply of Nvidia's RTX Blackwell GPUs in the third quarter of this year is below the second quarter, and that supply at the end of the year will be even lower than that. It also notes that this isn't purely down to the constrained supply of GPUs and memory owing to the demands of the data centre elites, but that other parts of the graphics card manufacturing process—such as PCBs and power componentry—are also suffering from long lead times compared with last year.
Given that Nvidia RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB and RTX 5070 graphics cards are both now batting around the $800 mark, it's mighty concerning that the more affordable end of the GPU spectrum look set to get slammed with higher prices, too. The doom disciple in me fears for a world where an RTX 5050 costs $500.
Though it can only cost $500 if someone is willing to pay that and surely, surely no-one would. Would they?
But it's not just going to be Nvidia cards though. It has been GeForce GPUs which have been affected more by the most recent price spike (though RX 9000 series cards have also had their fair share of price increases immediately after launch), but PC Partner is also the contract manufacturer of Sapphire GPUs, one of AMD's biggest graphics card makers, so I don't doubt it was talking to those cards, too. Especially if part of the supply constraints are around other components all GPUs need to live.
And if AMD cards get priced out of the reach of us mere PC gaming mortals, then there will be no alternatives for us.

title: Paradox commits a classic blunder and accidentally leaks its own post-apocalyptic grand strategy game
text:
As we head into big gaming week™ there are lots of studios with secret projects whirring behind the scenes, waiting to be announced at Gamescom or Opening Night Live. We now know that Paradox is one of said studios, thanks to its own forum filters.
"Paradox Forum website seems to accidentally list the unannounced game's name in the Unreleased Game filters," one eagle-eyed detective pointed out (via DualShockers ) on Reddit. In the accompanying screenshot you can see the keyword Afterworld appear beneath Unreleased Games and Prison Architect 2.
What is happening across the Paradox Universe? Find out more on Aug 25th @gamescom #gamescom #OpeningNightLive #CanYouGuessPDX👀 https://t.co/0FnSCPP0pC pic.twitter.com/2PWA9FBz1o August 21, 2026
Paradox has also been hinting at something appearing at Gamescom: "What is happening across the Paradox Universe?", a social media post reads. "Find out more on Aug 25th." And players seem to think Afterworld is set to be the big reveal.
Since then, online sleuths have been digging deeper. The Redditor who spotted the game name on the forums finally struck gold on Discord, finding the unreleased server , which had the following description: "Lead a tribe of survivors, rediscover ancient technology, manage wasteland settlements and wage wars of conquest and political struggle in Afterworld, an original post-apocalyptic survival grand strategy game." Sadly, the sleuthing stopped there: "Edit: rip they kicked me :(".
On the Paradox forums, there's a mix of speculation, a few reservations, and some disappointment that it's not the fantasy grand strategy game that a lot of folk were expecting. "To be honest: I would have liked a more fantasy based setting," one comment reads . "But ultimately the quality of a game is decided by mechanics and not by the setting."
Another forum member expressed concerns that it could go down the Fallout route, by treating "civilisation as a sort of 'one and done' endeavour and have the survivors forever picking at the corpse of the old world instead of ever making meaningful progress in building a new one."
It's worth reiterating that this is all based on one brief description, accompanied by some art, so it's a bit early to draw any conclusions. We'll likely find out more in the coming days, with Gamescom officially kicking off on Tuesday night with ONL.

title: 'The Guild' movie revival becomes highest-funded Kickstarter film ever, filling me with millennial nostalgia and making me very nervous
text:
As a millennial (boo, hiss) born in the 90s, I was just old enough to enjoy The Guild , a YouTube series about a group of dysfunctional MMO players, when it debuted online in 2007. 12-year-old me, who'd just gotten big into World of Warcraft and online games in general was downright invested—but that was then, and this is now.
I am currently 31 (also boo, also hiss) and I've got a lot less hair, which is part of why I was honestly surprised when I awoke to the news this week that The Guild: Ren Faire'd has become the highest-funded Kickstarter movie of all time—and one of the most successfully-funded movies to be fuelled by crowdfunding.
If you head on over to Kickstarter and apply the correct filters on its search function , you'll see it playing second fiddle to Critical Role: The Legend of Vox Machina 's animated "special"—which has since become a fully-fledged series spanning multiple seasons.
Originally asking for $1.5 million, the movie has brought in over $6.8 million at the time of writing. Now, this doesn't actually make it the highest-crowdfunded movie of all time by technicality —that award goes to 2025's David, which raised around $52 million, though that was achieved through asking for investors, rather than backers.
It was also based on a little book called The Bible, not a web series from 2007-2013 about World of Warcraft players. The Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit have a significant advantage when it comes to word of mouth.
"The Kickstarter is over. $6.8 million. You guys are incredible. Thank you for the support. The community. The creativity. We are so excited to make a movie and so much more for you guys," writes Felicia Day , who created the series itself. Day has since had a prolific career as an actress and the founder of Geek and Sundry, who we have to thank for the existence of Critical Role.
Which is cause for celebration! Though, I can't help but gnaw a little at my fingernails—The Guild was created originally in, quite literally, a different era, where MMOs were mysterious and inaccessible , and communities were more common. Heck, the OG series got picked up and streamed on Zune Marketplace and MSN Video. Remember those? I sure didn't.
And hey, maybe the Knights of Good going to the ren faire'll be a good laugh, but you'll either have to trade out most of the humour for jabs about how everything's on a Discord server now and high-end raids are datamined to death—or you'll have to become a little dated, only appealing to… well, people like me.
Which'll lead to three outcomes, two of which I dread: I'll be reminded of the sorry state of my favourite game genre by a bunch of actors who've aged better than me, I'll be mercilessly pandered to, or Felicia Day will successfully thread the needle and I'll have nothing to worry about. And hey, 45,500 people with $6.8 million bucks to spare aren't nearly as nervous. The Guild: Ren Faire'd plans to release sometime in 2027.

title: Both AMD and Intel's desktop CPU sales are falling off a cliff but Ryzen is falling a little slower
text:
Apart from the very occasional bundle , I can't remember the last time we recommended a deal on a CPU. Monitors, yes. Gaming PCs, definitely. But not CPUs, because however well-priced they are, it's hard to recommend a system upgrade when buying the rest of the system needed to go along with it is so damn expensive. I'm not entirely surprised, then, that Mercury Research says that desktop CPU shipments from AMD and Intel "in the second quarter are best described as ugly."
According to the market research firm, this is the case despite growth in the overall CPU market:
"In spite of a decidedly gloomy outlook on client processors from the suppliers for the second quarter, actual results for both X86 and ARM CPUs were up strongly in the second quarter of 2026, with sequential quarterly growth of the total market exceeding 10 percent, far in excess of normal seasonal trends which call for a slight decline in the quarter."
In other words, server and mobile (laptop) CPUs spanning x86 and ARM are doing well enough that the poor sales of x86 CPUs doesn't damage the overall CPU market picture.
But for us gamers, those x86 'client' CPUs are the important ones, as they're what sit inside our gaming rigs.
Mercury says: "while server and mobile CPU shipments had strong growth, desktop CPU shipments declined on top of an already poor first quarter, resulting in a large on-year downturn in excess of 20%. Both AMD and Intel experienced significant on-year weakness in desktop CPUs—with AMD having relatively smaller declines—however on a sequential basis AMD's declines were much smaller than Intel's. As a result AMD gained share both sequentially and on year in desktop CPUs, in spite of lower shipments."
In other words, both AMD's and Intel's desktop CPU sales seem to be falling down quite a steep hill, but Intel's are falling a little quicker, meaning AMD is technically scooping up more market share in this space. It's just that space itself is getting smaller.
(Image credit: Future) It's worth noting that a lot of these CPU shipments are likely those being packaged in pre-built OEM PCs or sent to system builders to be fitted in pre-built gaming PCs. Which means the numbers likely reflect not just a decline in people buying standalone CPUs, but people buying fewer full system upgrades, and system builders less interested in pallets full of the things. We've already seen corroboration that the number of worldwide PC shipments is falling .
And let's not forget that a lot of those who do buy a standalone CPU will be buying it alongside other components for a full system DIY upgrade. That means a motherboard, which is a reasonable cost; and RAM, which is absolutely not.
Given this, even if CPU prices remain stable, it's no surprise we're seeing fewer CPU shipments as more and more people are becoming reluctant to buy memory and storage at astronomical prices thanks to the global memory shortage .
It's also worth noting that although client laptop CPUs are doing well, that's not the case for everything in the world of portables. According to Counterpoint Research , for instance, the global smartphone market is expected to fall 14.3% this year due to cost pressures. The memory and component shortage, engendered by the AI server boom, is sure to keep affecting a whole bunch of products and industries. At least we only have to worry until, uhh, 2030 or beyond .

title: 《鸣潮》全球多市场App Store畅销榜单同步冲高！游戏开发者速看：二次元手游该如何兼顾用户回流、付费与留存？
text:
据悉，近日，库洛游戏旗下开放世界动作 RPG 手游《鸣潮》正式开启 3.6 版本。新版本上线新角色清宵、景燃以及新武器等，同时还加入了新主线剧情、新区域、限时活动等，并对多项游戏体验进行了优化升级。
七麦数据监测显示，8 月 20 日，《鸣潮》登上中国大陆 App Store 游戏畅销榜第 7 名、韩国游戏畅销榜第 1 名；在日本、印尼 iPhone 游戏畅销榜，分别攀升至第 9 名、第 7 名。
这组榜单排名虽然不能直接等同于该款产品的下载量或者收入，也不能说明本次版本更新直接影响了榜单排名上涨。但这份数据可以给我们带来一个思考： 一款已经步入长线运营阶段的游戏，该怎样通过大版本更新，同时实现用户回流、拉动付费、稳住用户留存。
《鸣潮》 更新3.6 版本，多市场榜单迎来攀升
《鸣潮》的 3.6 版本，并非简单上线两名新角色。根据 App Store 版本更新说明可以看到，除了上线五星角色、五星武器外，该版本还同步开放了新主线、新区域、新挑战和多项限时活动，并上线七日登录福利活动，降低老玩家回归门槛。
版本还针对游戏内的摩托导航与自动驾驶等方面进行了体验优化，同时调整了跨平台设备运行性能。这类改动不会直接制造出圈话题，但却会影响玩家回归后愿不愿意继续玩下去。
据七麦数据显示，该款游戏近一周在中国大陆 App Store 游戏畅销榜从第 102 升至第 7；在日本游戏畅销榜从第 63 升至第 9；在韩国游戏畅销榜最高从第 39 升至第 1。
《鸣潮》近日在中国大陆游戏畅销榜排名变化
同一时间，全球多市场都在《鸣潮》的版本更新周期内出现了排名明显上涨。可以看到，本次版本带来的市场反馈，并不是单一市场的个别现象。
同一时间段，“鸣潮清宵上线” 登上抖音热榜第 26 位。该热度仅代表国内社交平台的讨论热度，不能直接换算成下载和收入，但可以看出，新角色承担起版本对外传播的主要抓手。
大版本不是只上线新角色，还要把这条链路同时跑通
二次元游戏做大版本更新，很多团队习惯把绝大多数资源投入到新角色宣发上。 新角色确实能够带动社交讨论，制造付费转化的契机，但玩家完整体验是一整条连贯链路：被新角色吸引回坑，体验剧情与各类活动，最后决定要不要继续留下来。
《鸣潮》3.6 版本，把这条用户链路拆解得十分清晰。新角色与武器给玩家设立了明确的获取目标；新主线、新区域、各类活动补齐了游戏内容供给；登录福利降低了老玩家回归门槛；导航、功能推荐、性能优化，则提升了玩家游戏过程中的各类体验。
从中我们可以观察到，游戏大版本的商业化，不只是发生在付费环节，也体现在用户回流之后的每一处产品体验当中。
这也意味着增长团队要重视版本更新说明。它不只是一份功能更新清单，更是产品团队如何分配 “召回用户、拉长游戏时长、承接付费转化” 三类核心目标的公开参考。
推广人可以把大版本更新拆解成三层逻辑去落地。
第一层，搭建用户回流理由。 新剧情、新地图、限时活动、登录奖励，都要回答玩家一个核心问题：为什么我现在要回到游戏。如果活动带有明确时间周期，可以同步配置 App Store 应用内活动，在商店端同步传递出召回用户回归理由。
第二层，保持投放素材等的一致性。 新角色、新道具，要和游戏剧情、场景玩法做绑定，而不是单纯强调角色稀有度。商店产品页面、投放广告素材、游戏内入口，传递的信息要保持统一，降低用户点击跳转进游戏之后的心理落差。
第三层，做好用户留存理由。 导航、系统推荐、邮件、性能优化，虽然不像新角色那样容易受到玩家关注，却也会影响回流玩家会不会进行第二次打开。产品团队需要结合 App Analytics 以及自有后台数据，重点观察版本更新后的激活情况、关键任务完成率、回访数据，不要只盯着更新首日的榜单名次。
对于增长团队来说，多市场同步更新，不等于一套素材通用于全部地区。中国大陆、日本、韩国、印尼的市场环境和用户环境都存在差异。团队需要针对不同市场重新打磨商店产品页面第一屏卖点，再借助产品页面优化、自定产品页面，分别测试角色、剧情、活动不同的宣传方向，筛选出能够真正提升转化的方案。
结语
七麦数据结合多个市场 App Store 榜单、3.6 版本更新说明、官方维护公告以及社交平台热度观察发现，本次版本更新值得借鉴的点，并不是一次短期冲榜，而是一套完整的版本运营动作。
新角色可以带来话题度，吸引玩家注意力，新的游戏内容可以承接用户回流，体验优化可以保障用户留存。这三件事在同一个版本周期同步落地，使大版本能够同时触达新用户、回流老用户以及付费用户。
后续大家还可以持续关注这两点：版本活动首周过后，榜单热度能否维持；体验层面的优化，能不能转化成更加稳定的用户回访。
你的下一个大版本，是只准备一张新角色海报，还是搭建一整套完整的用户回归路径？
